resolutions.researcher_notes: No source states 'operating' verbatim, but both describe the line as actively carrying crude present-tense, 16 years apart: Apache's Feb 2004 EIA ('This crude oil line runs from Meliha to El Hamra terminal. It is owned and operated by Agiba Oil Company') and Egypt Oil & Gas's March 2020 Western Desert report, which tables it as one of the region's four currently-active crude pipelines with a live length/diameter/capacity figure. Status is inferable from continuous-operation prose across two independent eras, but kept at medium (not high) since neither states the word/status directly. url_verifier's automated substring screen returns 'missing expected' on both PDFs -- both are large, non-plain-text-encoded documents (121pp and a scanned-table layout respectively) that its extractor doesn't fully traverse; hand-confirmed via `pdftotext -layout` locally, which shows the relevant passages/table row clearly.

No source found states a start/commissioning year for this pipeline. WEPCO's own site says its Badr-1 operations have run 'since the early 1980s', which is directionally consistent with 1986 but too vague (could be 1980-1983) to cite as support for a specific year -- not treated as a match per the no-mismatched-value rule. thefreelibrary.com's Western Desert oil-fields piece (seed citation) 403s and could not be read.

VALUE CONFLICT, not sourced: Egypt Oil & Gas's March 2020 Western Desert report tables the Meleiha-El Hamra line's capacity as 90,000 bbl/d (same table gives length 167 km and diameter 16in, both matching the sheet), not the sheet's 140,000 bpd. Per the no-orphan-ref rule this is not cited as support for 140,000; flagging the disagreement for Update review instead. Source: https://egyptoil-gas.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/03/The-Western-Desert-Egypt%E2%80%99s-Giant-Petroleum-Reservoir-.pdf, table 'Crude Oil Infrastructure in the Western Desert', row 'Meleiha-El Hamra | Meleiha Fields | El Hamra | 167 | 16 | 90,000'.

Egypt Oil & Gas's March 2020 Western Desert report tables the Meleiha-El Hamra pipeline (From: Meleiha Fields, To: El Hamra) at Length 167 km -- exact match to the sheet. Only source found with a line-specific length figure, so single-source/medium. url_verifier's automated screen misses the match (large scanned-table PDF its extractor doesn't fully traverse); hand-confirmed via `pdftotext -layout`.

Apache's Feb 2004 EIA describes 'a 16" crude oil line [that] runs from Meliha to El Hamra terminal'. Egypt Oil & Gas's March 2020 report independently tables the same line's diameter as 16in. Two independent agreeing sources, 16 years apart. Both large PDFs url_verifier's automated screen doesn't fully traverse; hand-confirmed via `pdftotext -layout`.

Apache's 2004 EIA: 'This crude oil line runs from Meliha to El Hamra terminal.' Egypt Oil & Gas's 2020 report separately tables 'Meleiha Fields' as the pipeline's origin and, in its narrative section, places the Meleiha field 'in the northern part of the Western Desert, about 60 km south off Matruh City' -- consistent with the sheet's Matruh state/province. Two independent agreeing sources for both the Meleiha origin and its Matruh-area location; hand-confirmed via `pdftotext -layout` since both are large PDFs url_verifier's screen doesn't fully traverse.

Both the Apache 2004 EIA ('...to El Hamra terminal') and the Egypt Oil & Gas 2020 report (tabled endpoint 'El Hamra', and narratively 'El Hamra terminal is operated by the WEPCO') independently name El Hamra terminal as this line's endpoint. Neither source states the Matruh governorate specifically for El Hamra itself (only 'Western Desert'/coastal), so kept at medium for that sub-field despite two agreeing sources on the terminal name. Hand-confirmed via `pdftotext -layout` (both large PDFs url_verifier's screen doesn't fully traverse).

VALUE CONFLICT, not sourced: Apache's own 2004 EIA states this exact line ('a 16" crude oil line [that] runs from Meliha to El Hamra terminal') 'is owned and operated by Agiba Oil Company' -- not Apache Corp/EGPC as the sheet has it. Agiba Oil Company is itself a separate Eni/EGPC joint venture, distinct from Apache's own Khalda/Bapetco/Qarun JV family (per the same EIA and the Egypt Oil & Gas Western Desert report). Per the no-orphan-ref rule, not citing this as support; flagging the disagreement for Update review instead. Source: https://www.miga.org/documents/Apache_Egypt_2004_Egyptian_Oil_and_Gas_Activities_EIA.pdf, 'Project Description, Prepared by FIREBIRD, February 2004', section 1.15.
